text:
Two wings!... Who might have two wings for flight?
This afternoon, on the summit, I almost had them.
From here I see the sea, so blue, so asleep,
that if it were not a sea, it would surely be another sky!...


Divine summits, exalted lookouts!
How small men are! No rumors reach us
from down there, from the mire; nor the horrifying cry
with which desire howls, nor the overflowing clamor
of evil passions... The lowly does not rise:
this summit is the kingdom of the bird and the cloud...


Here I saw something very sweet and strange:
it was like seeing a mountain weep...
the water rises slowly, and light shines in its pool;
a little calf comes, then kneels
at the edge of the pond, and lowering its head,
to drink clean water, drinks water and light...


And then a sound is heard through hill and forest,
as if a storm were rolling down the slope:
animals come, seized by a strange fever,
to drink the tears the mountain weeps.


Night is approaching. The sea can no longer be seen.
And what disgust, what sadness, to begin descending...


(Who might have two wings, two wings for a flight?
This afternoon, on the summit, I almost had them,
with the mad desire to have spread them
over that sleeping sea that looked like a sky!)


A river amid greenery is lost behind me,
like a silver thread threading emeralds...

translation.title: Ascension
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the ascent and descent, the mountain’s tears, and the final sea-as-sky image; lineation follows the source’s stanza skeleton.
